# FluentReport

> .NET 10 library for generating PDF reports with a fluent C# API. The same document also renders to HTML (for email) and Excel, and RDLC / SSRS report definitions can be imported and rendered with data. Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux (including containers without fonts). MIT licensed, published on NuGet.

Facts to get right when writing code with FluentReport:

- Target framework: `net10.0`. Install only the output packages you need: `FluentReport` (PDF, SkiaSharp 4), `FluentReport.Html`, `FluentReport.Excel` (ClosedXML), `FluentReport.Rdlc` (RDLC import). `FluentReport.Core` (document model and fluent API) comes with any of them.
- Namespaces: `FluentReport` (`Document`, `GeneratePdf`, `PdfOptions`), `FluentReport.Core` (`PageSizes`), `FluentReport.Styling` (`ReportColor`, `TextStyle`), `FluentReport.Elements` (`ChartType`, element types), `FluentReport.Html` (`GenerateHtml`, `GenerateHtmlFragment`), `FluentReport.Excel` (`GenerateExcel`), `FluentReport.Rdlc` (`Document.FromRdlc`, `RdlcImportOptions`).
- Entry point: `Document.Create(container => container.Page(page => { page.Header()…; page.Content()…; page.Footer()…; }))`. Output: `doc.GeneratePdf(path | stream)` or `byte[] doc.GeneratePdf()`, `doc.GenerateHtml(...)`, `doc.GenerateHtmlFragment()`, `doc.GenerateExcel(...)`.
- Every container holds exactly one content element (`Text`, `Column`, `Row`, `Table`, `Image`, `List`, `Line`, `Spacer`, `Chart`, …); a second one throws `InvalidOperationException`. Use `Column(col => { col.Item()…; col.Item()…; })` or `Row(row => { row.RelativeItem()…; row.FixedItem(80)…; })` for several.
- Container decorators (`Padding`, `Background`, `Border`, `AlignCenter`) go before the content: `.Padding(5).Background("#EEEEEE").Text("x")`. Their order does not matter. Aligned text keeps its background and border as wide as the container (a shaded table header cell stays fully shaded); other aligned content shrinks to its width. After `.Text(...)` the chain is a `TextBuilder`: `.FontSize()`, `.Bold()`, `.Italic()`, `.Color()`, `.AlignRight()` style the text.
- Units are points (1/72 inch). Colors are `"#RRGGBB"` or `"#RRGGBBAA"` strings (the 3-digit `"#EEE"` form throws) or `ReportColor`.
- Tables: `ColumnsDefinition(c => { c.RelativeColumn(2); c.ConstantColumn(80); })`, then `Header(h => h.Cell()…)`, `table.Cell()` per data cell (cells wrap into rows by column count), optional `Footer(...)` and `BorderEachCell()`. In PDF, tables split across pages and repeat the header.
- Page numbers: `page.Footer().Text(x => { x.Span("Page "); x.CurrentPageNumber(); x.Span(" of "); x.TotalPages(); })`.
- Receipts on roll paper: `page.ContinuousSize(227)` (80 mm) makes one page as tall as its content instead of a fixed height.
- Fonts in PDF: the system font by default, the bundled DejaVu Sans when the system has none. For identical output everywhere pass `new PdfOptions { FontResolver = style => style.EffectiveBold ? boldTypeface : regularTypeface }` with `SKTypeface.FromFile(...)`.
- RDLC: `Document.FromRdlc(path, datasets: new Dictionary<string, IEnumerable<object>> { ["DataSetName"] = rows.Cast<object>() }, parameters: …, options: new RdlcImportOptions { Culture = new CultureInfo("es-UY") })`, then any `Generate*` method. Rows can be POCOs or dictionaries. Use `new RdlcDocumentFactory(...)` and its `Warnings` to see what was not supported.
- Command line, no project: `dnx FluentReport.Cli render report.rdlc --data DataSetName=rows.json -o out.pdf` (.NET 10 SDK; `-o` extension picks pdf, png, html or xlsx; `-p Name=value` for parameters; `--culture es-UY`). Rows are JSON arrays of objects.
- Excel skips images; charts, canvases and rotated text render a text fallback in HTML and Excel.

<!-- Source: README.md -->

# FluentReport

.NET 10 library for generating **PDF** reports with a fluent C# API, with the same document also rendering to **HTML / email** and **Excel**, and an importer for **RDLC / SSRS** report definitions. Linux compatible.

## Packages

| Package | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| [`FluentReport`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/FluentReport) | PDF renderer (SkiaSharp) with real pagination |
| [`FluentReport.Html`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/FluentReport.Html) | HTML / email renderer (table layout, inline styles) |
| [`FluentReport.Excel`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/FluentReport.Excel) | Excel (.xlsx) renderer (ClosedXML) |
| [`FluentReport.Rdlc`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/FluentReport.Rdlc) | RDLC / SSRS importer |
| [`FluentReport.Core`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/FluentReport.Core) | Document model and fluent API, brought in by the packages above |
| [`FluentReport.Cli`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/FluentReport.Cli) | Command-line tool: renders RDLC reports with JSON data, no project needed |

```shell
dotnet add package FluentReport          # PDF
dotnet add package FluentReport.Html     # + HTML / email
dotnet add package FluentReport.Excel    # + Excel
dotnet add package FluentReport.Rdlc     # + RDLC import
```

## Quick start

```csharp
using FluentReport;
using FluentReport.Core;

var doc = Document.Create(container =>
{
    container.Page(page =>
    {
        page.Size(PageSizes.A4);
        page.MarginAll(40);

        page.Header().Text("My Report").FontSize(20).Bold().AlignCenter();

        page.Content().Column(col =>
        {
            col.Spacing(8);
            col.Item().Text("Summary").FontSize(14).Bold();
            col.Item().Line(1);
            col.Item().Table(table =>
            {
                table.ColumnsDefinition(cols => { cols.RelativeColumn(2); cols.RelativeColumn(1); });
                table.Header(h =>
                {
                    h.Cell().Background("#4472C4").Padding(5).Text("Product").Bold().Color("#FFFFFF");
                    h.Cell().Background("#4472C4").Padding(5).Text("Price").Bold().Color("#FFFFFF");
                });
                table.Cell().Padding(5).Text("Widget A");
                table.Cell().Padding(5).Text("9.99").AlignRight();
                table.Footer(f =>
                {
                    f.Cell().Padding(5).Text("Total").Bold();
                    f.Cell().Padding(5).Text("9.99").Bold().AlignRight();
                });
            });
        });

        page.Footer().AlignCenter().Text(x =>
        {
            x.Span("Page "); x.CurrentPageNumber(); x.Span(" of "); x.TotalPages();
        }).FontSize(8);
    });
});

doc.GeneratePdf("report.pdf");
```

The same `doc` renders to the other formats:

```csharp
using FluentReport.Excel;
using FluentReport.Html;

doc.GenerateHtml("report.html");
string emailBody = doc.GenerateHtmlFragment();
doc.GenerateExcel("report.xlsx");
```

Long content paginates on its own: columns split between items (also when nested or decorated), text between lines, and tables between rows with the header repeated on every page.

### RDLC

```csharp
using System.Globalization;
using FluentReport.Rdlc;

var invoice = Document.FromRdlc(
    "reports/invoice.rdlc",
    datasets: new Dictionary<string, IEnumerable<object>> { ["Lines"] = lines.Cast<object>() },
    options: new RdlcImportOptions { Culture = new CultureInfo("es-UY") });

invoice.GeneratePdf("invoice.pdf");
```

### Command line

`FluentReport.Cli` renders an RDLC report with JSON data from the terminal, with no project to
create. With the .NET 10 SDK, `dnx` runs it without installing it:

```shell
dnx FluentReport.Cli render invoice.rdlc --data Lines=lines.json --culture es-UY -o invoice.pdf
```

The extension of `-o` picks the format (`.pdf`, `.png`, `.html`, `.xlsx`). Each dataset takes an
array of JSON objects, one per row; `-p Name=value` sets report parameters. To call it as
`fluentreport`, install it once with `dotnet tool install -g FluentReport.Cli`. Every option is in
[its README](https://github.com/MathiasGonzalez/FluentReport/blob/main/src/FluentReport.Cli/README.md).

## Renderer support

| Feature | PDF | HTML | Excel |
|---------|:---:|:----:|:-----:|
| Text, fonts, colors, alignment, rich text | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Page numbers | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Column / Row layout | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ (merged cells) |
| Tables: header, footer, column spans, borders | ✓ (split across pages) | ✓ | ✓ |
| Lists | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP) | ✓ | ✓ (data URI) | — |
| Backgrounds, borders, padding | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ (no padding) |
| Charts, canvas, rotated text | ✓ | fallback | fallback |
| Pagination / page breaks | ✓ | ✓ (divider) | ✓ (worksheets) |
| Custom fonts | ✓ | font-family | font name |

Output does not depend on the machine's regional settings: CSS numbers always use `.`, and the RDLC importer formats values with an explicit culture.

### Example output — e-Factura (Uruguay)

See the generated files in [`samples/FluentReport.Samples/output`](https://github.com/MathiasGonzalez/FluentReport/blob/main/samples/FluentReport.Samples/output) ([invoice](https://github.com/MathiasGonzalez/FluentReport/blob/main/samples/FluentReport.Samples/output/05-invoice.pdf), [salary slip](https://github.com/MathiasGonzalez/FluentReport/blob/main/samples/FluentReport.Samples/output/10-recibo-sueldo.pdf), …) and [the UY samples guide](https://github.com/MathiasGonzalez/FluentReport/blob/main/docs/uy-fiscal-samples.md).

- [ClosedXML](https://www.nuget.org/packages/ClosedXML) 0.105.1 — Excel rendering

<!-- Source: docs/api.md -->

# FluentReport — API Reference

> **Required namespaces**
> ```csharp
> using FluentReport;           // Document, GeneratePdf (FluentReport package)
> using FluentReport.Core;      // PageSizes, DocumentSettings
> using FluentReport.Elements;  // ChartType
> using FluentReport.Styling;   // ReportColor, TextStyle
> using FluentReport.Html;      // GenerateHtml (FluentReport.Html package)
> using FluentReport.Excel;     // GenerateExcel (FluentReport.Excel package)
> using FluentReport.Rdlc;      // Document.FromRdlc (FluentReport.Rdlc package)
> ```

---

## Document

| Member | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `Document.Create(Action<DocumentBuilder>)` | Builds a document with the fluent API. At least one page is required. |
| `Document.FromSettings(DocumentSettings)` | Wraps a model built by hand or by an importer. At least one page is required. |
| `.Settings` | The document model (`DocumentSettings` → pages → elements). |
| `.GeneratePdf(path\|stream\|—, options?)` | PDF *(FluentReport)* — see [PDF output](#pdf-output). |
| `.GenerateImages(scale = 1, options?)` | One PNG per page *(FluentReport)*. |
| `.GetPdfPageCount(options?)` | Number of PDF pages *(FluentReport)*. |
| `.GenerateHtml(path\|stream\|—, options?)` | Full HTML document *(FluentReport.Html)*. |
| `.GenerateHtmlFragment(options?)` | HTML fragment for an email body *(FluentReport.Html)*. |
| `.GenerateExcel(path\|stream\|—)` | `.xlsx` workbook *(FluentReport.Excel)*. |
| `Document.FromRdlc(path, …)` / `FromRdlcStream` / `FromRdlcXml` | RDLC import *(FluentReport.Rdlc)* — see [RDLC import](#rdlc-import). |

---

## DocumentBuilder

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `.Page(Action<PageBuilder>)` | Adds a page section. In PDF its content flows over as many pages as needed with the header and footer repeated; in HTML each section is a block separated by a divider; in Excel a worksheet. |

## PageBuilder

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `.Size(PageSize)` / `.Size(float width, float height)` | Page size in points (1 pt = 1/72 in). |
| `.ContinuousSize(float width)` | A page that grows to the height of its content: everything on one page, with no blank space below. For receipts on roll paper (80 mm ≈ 227 pt). Page breaks are ignored. PDF and PNG. |
| `.Landscape()` | Swaps width and height. |
| `.MarginAll(float)` / `.Margin(top, right, bottom, left)` / `.MarginHorizontal(float)` / `.MarginVertical(float)` | Margins in points; in HTML they become cell padding. |
| `.Header()` / `.Content()` / `.Footer()` | Return the `ContainerBuilder` of each region. |

```csharp
container.Page(page =>
{
    page.Size(PageSizes.A4);
    page.MarginAll(40);

    page.Header().Text("My Report").FontSize(16).Bold().AlignCenter();
    page.Content().Column(col => { col.Spacing(8); col.Item().Text("..."); });
    page.Footer().AlignCenter().Text(x =>
    {
        x.Span("Page "); x.CurrentPageNumber(); x.Span(" of "); x.TotalPages();
    });
});
```

`CurrentPageNumber()` / `TotalPages()` resolve to the document page and the page count (in Excel: the worksheet's page).

---

## ContainerBuilder

Every region, column/row item and table cell is a `ContainerBuilder`. It holds **one** content element; calling a second content method throws `InvalidOperationException` — use `Column()` or `Row()` to place several elements.

### Content

| Method | Returns | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `.Text(string)` | `TextBuilder` | Text. |
| `.Text(Action<DynamicTextBuilder>)` | `TextBuilder` | Text made of spans (mixed styles, page numbers). |
| `.Column(Action<ColumnBuilder>)` | `ContainerBuilder` | Vertical stack. |
| `.Row(Action<RowBuilder>)` | `ContainerBuilder` | Horizontal stack. |
| `.Table(Action<TableBuilder>)` | `ContainerBuilder` | Table. |
| `.List<T>(items, template, spacing = 0)` | `ContainerBuilder` | One item per element of `items`, stacked vertically. |
| `.Image(string path)` / `.Image(byte[])` | `ContainerBuilder` | PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or BMP. `Image(path)` throws if the file does not exist. HTML embeds it as a data URI; Excel skips images. Size: natural size (1 px = 1 pt) capped to the width; a single fixed side keeps the aspect ratio. |
| `.Spacer(float height = 0)` | `ContainerBuilder` | Empty vertical space. |
| `.Line(float thickness = 1, string? colorHex = null)` | `ContainerBuilder` | Horizontal rule. |
| `.PageBreak()` | `ContainerBuilder` | New page in PDF (at any depth); a divider in HTML; a new worksheet in Excel (top level of `Content()`). |
| `.Chart()` | `ChartBuilder` | Bar or line chart (PDF; HTML/Excel render its fallback). |
| `.Subreport(Document)` | `ContainerBuilder` | Inserts the content of another document's pages (headers/footers not repeated). |
| `.Canvas(width, height, (SKCanvas, SKRect) => …)` | `ContainerBuilder` | Custom vector drawing, PDF only *(FluentReport)*. |
| `.Element(IElement)` | `ContainerBuilder` | Custom element (the renderer must know it). |

### Decorators

Order-independent; they can be called before or after the content method, and in any order. They always nest the same way: padding around the content, background and border around the padding, alignment outermost. Aligned text keeps a background and border as wide as its container, so `.Background(..).Padding(4).AlignCenter().Text(..)` shades the whole table cell; other aligned content (an image, a column) is shrunk to its own width together with its background and border.

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `.Padding(float)`, `.PaddingHorizontal/Vertical(float)`, `.PaddingTop/Bottom/Left/Right(float)` | Padding. |
| `.Background(string hex)` / `.Background(ReportColor)` | Background color (padding included). |
| `.Border(float width = 1, string? colorHex = null)` | Border (padding included). |
| `.AlignLeft()` / `.AlignCenter()` / `.AlignRight()` | Horizontal position of the content. Text is aligned line by line; other content is shrunk to its width and moved. |

```csharp
col.Item()
   .Background("#E8F4FD")
   .Border(1, "#2196F3")
   .Padding(8)
   .AlignCenter()
   .Text("Highlighted").Bold();
```

---

## TextBuilder

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `.FontSize(float)` | Size in points (HTML uses the same number in px). |
| `.FontFamily(string)` | Font family. |
| `.Bold()` / `.Italic()` / `.Underline()` | Weight and decoration. |
| `.Color(string hex)` / `.Color(ReportColor)` | Text color. |
| `.AlignLeft()` / `.AlignCenter()` / `.AlignRight()` / `.AlignJustify()` | Text alignment (inside a table cell it aligns the cell). |
| `.LineSpacing(float)` | Line height multiplier (default `1.2`). |
| `.Rotate(float degrees)` | Rotation, counter-clockwise. PDF only; layout uses the unrotated box. |

The style applies to every span of `Text(x => …)` as well; a span's own settings win:

```csharp
page.Footer().Text(x =>
{
    x.Span("Page ");
    x.CurrentPageNumber(s => s.Bold = true);
}).FontSize(8).Color("#666666");   // both spans are 8 pt grey; the number is also bold
```

## DynamicTextBuilder

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `.Span(string, Action<TextStyle>? = null)` | Text span. |
| `.CurrentPageNumber(Action<TextStyle>? = null)` | Current page number. |
| `.TotalPages(Action<TextStyle>? = null)` | Page count. |

---

## ColumnBuilder / RowBuilder

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `ColumnBuilder.Spacing(float)` / `.Item()` | Gap between items; adds an item. |
| `RowBuilder.Spacing(float)` | Gap between items. |
| `RowBuilder.RelativeItem(float weight = 1)` / `.Item()` | Proportional width. |
| `RowBuilder.FixedItem(float width)` | Fixed width in points. |

---

## TableBuilder

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `.ColumnsDefinition(c => c.RelativeColumn(w) / c.ConstantColumn(pt))` | Columns and their widths. |
| `.Header(h => h.Cell(colSpan))` | Header rows (`<thead>`, bold in Excel). |
| `.Cell(int colSpan = 1)` | Data cell. |
| `.Footer(f => f.Cell(colSpan))` | Rows after the data (totals, notes): `<tfoot>` in HTML. |
| `.BorderEachCell(float width = 1, string? colorHex = null)` | Border on every cell. |

Cells are listed left-to-right, top-to-bottom and wrap into rows automatically, respecting `colSpan`.

```csharp
col.Item().Table(table =>
{
    table.ColumnsDefinition(cols => { cols.RelativeColumn(3); cols.ConstantColumn(80); });
    table.Header(h =>
    {
        h.Cell().Background("#4472C4").Padding(5).Text("Product").Bold().Color("#FFFFFF");
        h.Cell().Background("#4472C4").Padding(5).Text("Price").Bold().Color("#FFFFFF");
    });
    foreach (var item in products)
    {
        table.Cell().Padding(4).Text(item.Name);
        table.Cell().Padding(4).Text(item.Price.ToString("N2")).AlignRight();
    }
    table.Footer(f =>
    {
        f.Cell().Padding(4).Text("Total").Bold();
        f.Cell().Padding(4).Text(total.ToString("N2")).Bold().AlignRight();
    });
    table.BorderEachCell(0.5f, "#CCCCCC");
});
```

---

## ChartBuilder

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `.Type(ChartType.Bar \| ChartType.Line)` | Chart type. |
| `.Title(string)` / `.Height(float)` | Title; height in points (default 200). |
| `.Categories(IEnumerable<string>)` | X-axis labels. |
| `.AddSeries(label, values, colorHex?)` | Data series; color defaults to a palette. Bars grow from zero, so negative values point down. |
| `.Fallback(string)` | Text HTML and Excel show instead of the chart. |

---

## Styling

`ReportColor` (in `FluentReport.Styling`): `new ReportColor(r, g, b[, a])`, `ReportColor.FromHex("#RRGGBB" | "#RRGGBBAA")`, constants `Black`, `White`, `Gray`, `LightGray`, `Transparent`.

`TextStyle` properties: `FontSize` (12), `FontFamily` ("sans-serif" → the HTML font option), `Bold`, `Italic`, `Underline`, `Color`, `Alignment`, `LineSpacing` (1.2), `Rotation` (PDF only), and the optional `BoldResolver`, `ItalicResolver`, `ColorResolver` delegates that override the static value when the document is rendered.

`PageSizes`: `A3`, `A4`, `A5`, `Letter`, `Legal`.

---

## PDF output

Content flows across pages: columns split between items (also nested or inside padding/background/border), text between lines, and tables between rows, repeating header rows and keeping footer rows on the last page. Rows, images, charts and canvases move to the next page whole; one taller than a page is cut at the footer.

`PdfOptions`:

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `FontResolver` | `Func<TextStyle, SKTypeface?>` — e.g. embedded fonts. Return `null` for the system font. Typefaces are cached per render and never disposed. |
| `SubsetFonts` | Embed only the glyphs the document uses instead of whole font files (default `true`). Applies to TrueType fonts; others are embedded whole. |
| `Title` / `Author` | PDF metadata. |
| `MaxImagePixels` | Largest image decoded, in pixels (default 100 MP). Larger images throw `InvalidOperationException` before they are decoded, so a small compressed file cannot use gigabytes of memory. `null` removes the limit. |

Fonts are subset: a PDF carries only the glyphs it uses, a few tens of KB per face instead of several hundred. Fonts with CFF outlines and variable fonts are embedded whole.

When neither the resolver nor the system provides a usable font (typical on Linux and in containers without fonts), FluentReport uses its bundled DejaVu Sans (regular and bold; italic is synthesized). Use `FontResolver` for the same output on every machine.

---

## Renderer options

`HtmlRendererOptions`: `MaxWidth` (600 px, `null` = 100 %), `FontFamily` (default font stack), `PageDividerStyle`, `OutlookCompatible`.

Numbers in the generated CSS always use `.` as decimal separator, whatever the machine culture.

A custom `IElement` that a renderer does not know throws `NotSupportedException` instead of being dropped; an `IRendererSpecificElement` (charts, canvases) renders its `Fallback` in renderers that cannot draw it.

---

## RDLC import

```csharp
using FluentReport.Rdlc;

var doc = Document.FromRdlc(
    "reports/catalog.rdlc",
    datasets: new Dictionary<string, IEnumerable<object>> { ["Products"] = products.Cast<object>() },
    parameters: new Dictionary<string, object> { ["Company"] = "Acme Corp." },
    options: new RdlcImportOptions { Culture = new CultureInfo("es-UY") });

doc.GeneratePdf("catalog.pdf");
```

| Entry point | Source |
|-------------|--------|
| `Document.FromRdlc(path, datasets?, parameters?, globals?, options?)` | File |
| `Document.FromRdlcStream(stream, …)` | Stream |
| `Document.FromRdlcXml(xml, …)` | XML string |
| `new RdlcDocumentFactory(…).ParseFromFile/Stream/Xml(…)` | Same, plus `factory.Warnings` |

Rows can be POCOs or dictionaries; field names are case-insensitive.

Tablix row groups render a header and subtotal per group, with their sort expressions and filters. Aggregates without a scope argument cover the current detail row, group or table, as in SSRS; name a group, table or dataset to aggregate over it. `Globals!PageNumber` / `TotalPages` become page-number spans, so page headers and footers show real page numbers.

`RdlcImportOptions`:

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `Culture` | report `<Language>`, else invariant | Formats values and reads numbers/dates given as text. Never the machine culture. |
| `LoadExternalImages` | `true` | Load `<Image Source="External">`. |
| `ExternalImageDirectory` | the `.rdlc` folder (file import only) | External images are read only from inside this directory. |
| `StrictExpressions` | `false` | Throw instead of rendering empty text for unsupported expressions. |

Supported report items, expressions and known limitations: [rdlc-limitations.md](https://github.com/MathiasGonzalez/FluentReport/blob/main/docs/rdlc-limitations.md).


---

<!-- Source: docs/rdlc-limitations.md -->

# FluentReport.Rdlc — Supported features and limitations

`FluentReport.Rdlc` turns an `.rdlc` (SSRS 2005 / 2008+) definition and its data into a `Document` that renders to PDF, HTML and Excel. Anything it cannot import is listed (once) in `RdlcDocumentFactory.Warnings`; with `RdlcImportOptions.StrictExpressions` unsupported expressions throw instead.

## Report items

| RDLC item | Imported as | Notes |
|-----------|-------------|-------|
| `<Textbox>` | `TextElement` | Value or `<Paragraphs>/<TextRuns>` (one span per run). FontSize, FontFamily, FontWeight, FontStyle, TextDecoration, Color, TextAlign (textbox or paragraph), BackgroundColor, Padding, borders, `Format`. Style values can be expressions. |
| `<Rectangle>` | `ColumnElement` in a border/background | Its items are laid out like the body; the designed height is kept when it is taller than the content. |
| `<Line>` | `LineElement` | Color and width (`Border` or legacy `BorderWidth`). |
| `<Image>` | `ImageElement` | `Embedded`, `Database` (bytes or base64) and `External` (local file inside `ExternalImageDirectory`; URLs are not fetched). Only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and BMP are rendered. `Sizing`: `Fit` stretches to the item's box, `FitProportional` fits inside it keeping the aspect ratio, `AutoSize` (the default) uses the natural size from the pixels and resolution (96 dpi when the file has none), `Clip` uses the natural size scaled down to the box (it is not cropped). |
| `<Tablix>` (table, list) | `TableElement` | Row groups, details, sorting, filters, hidden rows/columns, `ColSpan`, `NoRowsMessage`. See below. |
| `<PageHeader>` / `<PageFooter>` | page header / footer | `Globals!PageNumber` / `TotalPages` render the real page numbers. |
| `<Page>` | page size and margins | |
| `<Chart>`, `<Subreport>`, gauges, maps | — | Skipped and reported in `Warnings`. |

Absolute positions are approximated: items whose `Top` is within 2 pt are placed side by side in a row (horizontal gaps kept), and vertical gaps of 6 pt or more become spacers. `PageBreak` with `Start` / `End` / `StartAndEnd` on a body item adds a page break.

### Styles

- **Format**: the `Format` style property (on the text run, else the textbox) is applied to numbers and dates with the import culture, e.g. `N2`, `C`, `#,0.00`, `dd/MM/yyyy`. Text values are left as they are.
- **Borders**: `Border` plus `TopBorder` / `RightBorder` / `BottomBorder` / `LeftBorder` (RDL 2008+) and `BorderStyle` / `BorderColor` / `BorderWidth` (RDL 2005). Every style other than `None` is drawn solid. In tables, cell borders line up into a grid.
- **Visibility**: `<Visibility><Hidden>` (literal or expression) on report items, tablix row members and tablix column members. Hidden items take no space. Toggles (`ToggleItem`, drill-down) keep their initial state, as in an exported report.
- Not imported: `VerticalAlign`, `LineHeight`, `WritingMode`, `CanGrow`/`CanShrink` (text always grows), border styles (dotted, dashed, double), `ToolTip`, actions (hyperlinks, drillthrough, bookmarks).
- **Fonts**: `FontFamily` is resolved from the fonts installed on the machine; a missing font (e.g. Calibri or Poppins on a Linux server) falls back to the default font, which changes text widths. Supply the font files with `PdfOptions.FontResolver`. Carlito is a free font metrically compatible with Calibri.

## Tablix

The row hierarchy is walked the way SSRS does:

- Static rows before the first group are the table header, repeated on every page. Static rows after the last group are the footer (grand totals), shown once at the end.
- A group with `<GroupExpressions>` renders once per distinct value, in first-appearance order or by its `<SortExpressions>`. Its static child rows (group header, subtotal) render once per group. Aggregates in them cover that group's rows.
- A details group (`<Group>` without expressions) renders once per row. `SortExpressions` on the member or on the tablix order the rows.
- `<Filters>` on the dataset, the tablix and groups: `Equal`, `NotEqual`, `GreaterThan(OrEqual)`, `LessThan(OrEqual)`, `In` (multi-value parameters included), `Between`, `Like`. `TopN`/`BottomN`/`TopPercent`/`BottomPercent` are reported and ignored.
- A tablix nested inside a group cell (e.g. a list with an inner table) shows the rows of that group when it uses the same dataset.

Not supported: column groups (matrix) — the columns are rendered once and a warning is reported; `RowSpan`; page breaks between group instances; `RepeatOnNewPage`/`KeepWithGroup` (the header always repeats).

## Expressions

Values keep their type (number, date, boolean, text) while an expression is evaluated; they become text at the end, formatted with the import culture (`RdlcImportOptions.Culture`, else the report `<Language>`, else invariant — never the machine's regional settings). Text comparisons and sorting use the same culture's collation.

| Kind | Supported |
|------|-----------|
| References | `Fields!X.Value` (through the field's `DataField`, or its `Value` for calculated fields), `Parameters!X.Value` / `.Label`, `Globals!X(.Value)` |
| Literals | strings, numbers, `True`, `False`, `Nothing` |
| Operators | `^ * / \ Mod + - &`, `= <> < > <= >=`, `Is` / `IsNot` (e.g. `Fields!X.Value Is Nothing`), `Not And AndAlso Or OrElse Xor` |
| Conditionals | `IIF`, `Switch`, `Choose` |
| Formatting | `Format` (.NET and VB named formats such as `"Currency"`, `"Short Date"`), `FormatNumber`, `FormatCurrency`, `FormatPercent` |
| Conversion / text | `CStr`, `CInt`, `CLng`, `CDec`, `CDbl`, `CBool`, `CDate`, `Len`, `Trim`, `LTrim`, `RTrim`, `UCase`, `LCase`, `Left`, `Right`, `Mid`, `Replace`, `IsNothing`, `Now`, `Today` |
| Aggregates | `Sum`, `Count`, `CountDistinct`, `CountRows`, `Avg`/`Average`, `Min`, `Max`, `First`, `Last` |
| Row functions | `RowNumber`, `RunningValue(expr, Sum, scope)`, `Previous` |

`Is Nothing` and `IsNothing(...)` are true only for a missing value (`null`, `DBNull`), not for an empty string, as in VB.

Aggregate scope follows SSRS: without a scope argument an aggregate covers the current scope — the row in a detail row, the group in a group header or footer, the tablix in its header or footer, the only dataset outside a tablix. A scope argument may name a group, a tablix or a dataset. `RowNumber` and `RunningValue` count rows in the order they are displayed.

Globals: `PageNumber`, `TotalPages` (and `Overall…`) become page-number spans resolved at render time. `ExecutionTime` defaults to the import time and `ReportName` to the file name. Other globals come from the `globals` dictionary, which also overrides these defaults.

Not supported (reported as warnings): `Lookup`, `LookupSet`, `MultiLookup`, `ReportItems!`, `User!`, custom code (`Code.`), `InScope`, `Level`, and other VB functions. Page numbers used inside arithmetic or `Format` are not computed.

## Other limitations

- `<Body><Height>` is ignored; content height follows the content.
- Each `<ReportSection>` becomes a page.
- Reflection is used for POCO rows; for trimmed/AOT apps use dictionary rows.
- The HTML renderer does not draw borders on table cells (PDF does).

## Limits for untrusted reports

- DTDs are rejected (`XmlException`): RDLC never uses them, and they are how XXE and entity-expansion attacks work.
- Documents nested more than 256 elements deep are rejected (`InvalidOperationException`). A tablix inside a rectangle is about 30 levels.
- Expressions with more than 100 nested parentheses, function calls, `Not` or signs, or more than 500 chained operators, evaluate to empty with a warning (or throw with `StrictExpressions`).
- External images that go through a symbolic link are not loaded.

See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/MathiasGonzalez/FluentReport/blob/main/SECURITY.md) for the full list.


---

<!-- Source: SECURITY.md -->

# Security

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report vulnerabilities privately through [GitHub security advisories](https://github.com/MathiasGonzalez/FluentReport/security/advisories/new). Do not open a public issue. Include the package, version and a minimal input that reproduces the problem.

Fixes are released for the latest major version.

## Processing untrusted input

FluentReport can render report definitions (`.rdlc`) and images that come from users. The packages are built so that hostile input fails with a catchable exception or a warning, instead of reading files, running code or taking the process down:

| Input | Protection |
|-------|------------|
| RDLC XML | DTDs are rejected, so external entities (XXE) and entity expansion never run. Documents nested more than 256 elements deep are rejected. |
| RDLC `<Code>` blocks and custom assemblies | Never executed. Expressions can call only the built-in functions and read public properties of the data rows. |
| RDLC expressions | More than 100 nested parentheses/calls or more than 500 chained operators produce a warning (an exception with `StrictExpressions`). |
| RDLC `Like` filters | Evaluated in linear time. |
| External images in RDLC | Only local files inside `ExternalImageDirectory` (by default the `.rdlc` folder, and none for streams and strings). URLs, paths outside the directory and symbolic links are ignored with a warning. Set `LoadExternalImages = false` to disable them. |
| Images in PDF | Images above `PdfOptions.MaxImagePixels` (100 megapixels by default) throw before they are decoded. |
| Very deep element trees | Building and rendering throw `InsufficientExecutionStackException` instead of overflowing the stack. |
| Text in HTML output | HTML-encoded; font names are filtered and colours are emitted as hex. |
| Text in Excel output | Written as text values, never as formulas. |

Rendering still takes time and memory proportional to the data. When the input is untrusted, run it with a timeout and limit the size of uploaded files and datasets.
